dossier.architecture: Low-electronics frame and belted elevator with combined coral/algae manipulation.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve frame uses corner trusses and underside electronics; added shielding after riding onto algae.
subsystems.intake: Station funnel; curved-rack algae collector added after prior event.
subsystems.transfer: Funnel supplies manipulator; separate storage permits coral/algae overlap.
subsystems.scoring: Elevator derived from 2024 design with wider belt and linked gearbox; carriage-mounted motors reduce distal arm mass.
subsystems.endgame: Funnel back wall doubles as cage capture; changed to one-bar engagement with polycarbonate guide and latch.
subsystems.controls: Safe-move cases coordinate arm/elevator; operator-selectable reef-side alignment.

versions: Added algae collector and one-bar climb revision.
Constant-force spring restrains energy chain after breakage and interference.
dossier.analysis: Endgame volume can overlap acquisition volume if the game permits sequential use. Sharing that space requires intentional cage clearance and wire routing rather than treating the climber as a final attachment.

context_documents.title: 2025-1706 · Cable control and a later algae arm are essential version details
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1706: Cable control and a later algae arm are essential version details

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The robot retains an elevator-based station-fed scorer and later adds a compact curved-rack algae intake. A constant-force spring pulls the elevator cable carrier inward after it repeatedly broke, flopped outward or entered the funnel. The climber uses the funnel’s rear region and was revised to grab one cage bar.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team describes the algae arm as lightweight and quick to deploy, and identifies the spring as the response to cable-carrier failures. The updated climb seeks easier capture rather than a larger nominal grasp.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A cable carrier is a moving structural interface, not an afterthought in the electrical system. Its force, bend radius and free envelope affect elevator current and what can enter the station funnel. An added algae collector also changes the safe pose space of an already working scorer. The architecture should retain the dated add-on history rather than imply the final robot existed at the first event.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Run full-stroke cable fatigue tests and check the spring at maximum extension. Test coral loading with the algae mechanism deployed and verify cage capture under angular misalignment.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/SvBYbyf57zo](https://youtu.be/SvBYbyf57zo)

source_reviews.title: Ratchet Rockers Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Retained dossier and supplement read. Interview captions not retrieved in this review.
facts: Prior notes describe a station-fed elevator, cable-carrier restraint, a later curved-rack algae arm and one-bar cage capture.
source_reviews.limitations: Mechanical details are inherited and need primary confirmation.

source_reviews.title: FIRST Event Web, Team 1706
source_reviews.review_basis: Read official team and event text.
facts: Robot name RIOT. Iowa Regional Innovation in Control Award.

source_reviews.title: FRC1706 interview announcement
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team's public announcement text.
facts: The team identifies its students as presenters of the 2025 design and functionality.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: RIOT is a station-fed elevator scorer in the retained account. The useful packaging question is whether three systems can occupy the funnel neighborhood at different times without degrading coral acquisition. Coral traverses it, the moving harness can intrude on it, and the climb uses its rear region. The later algae module adds an independent reach task and a new collision state. Treat this as a versioned architecture until the team interview or CAD can substantiate which parts ran together.
piece_flow: Station funnel feeds the coral manipulator, which moves with the elevator and arm.
A later curved-rack collector adds an algae path. The retained dossier describes separate retention that permits some overlap of tasks.
Endgame changes the use of the funnel's rear region from intake structure to cage approach and capture.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The dossier describes underside electronics and a low frame with corner trusses. This frees space above the deck but makes clearance over algae and access from below relevant. A harness controlled across the full elevator stroke has to stay clear of the funnel even with the arm rotating. At endgame the cage approach needs a clear sweep for both capture and the suspended robot.

subsystems.name: Funnel and coral scorer
subsystems.construction: Retained account describes a fixed station funnel and a belted elevator with arm actuation carried on the carriage.
subsystems.operation: Receive coral at the loading pose, then move the carriage and arm to place it.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior notes describe a wider belt and reuse of 2024 elevator design work.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Carriage-mounted actuation can reduce distal inertia while adding mass the elevator must lift on every cycle. Match current draw and reversal behavior matter more than static reach alone.
subsystems.interfaces: Funnel exit, gripper mouth and moving harness share the loading region.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect the loaded entrance with the elevator below and above its nominal transfer pose. Check whether reverse rollers can clear a pipe before raising.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact capture sensing, belt reeving and ratios.

subsystems.name: Cable carrier and added algae collector
subsystems.construction: Retained notes identify a constant-force spring on the carrier and a compact curved-rack algae collector.
subsystems.operation: The spring pulls the free carrier loop inward during travel. The collector adds a separate deploy and retract path.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior supplement reports harness breakage and funnel interference, and describes the algae arm as lightweight and quick to deploy.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Restraining the cable loop trades uncontrolled sweep for a persistent load and another fatigue component. The rack's available clearance needs checking at intermediate elevator heights.
subsystems.interfaces: Harness bend radius, rack envelope and coral path must work concurrently for the claimed overlap.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Cycle the harness under vibration and at maximum travel. Test a bent guard and algae-arm interruption while coral is loaded.
subsystems.unknowns: Spring rating, bracket geometry and algae retention sequence.

subsystems.name: Cage capture
subsystems.construction: Retained notes describe a polycarbonate guide and latch at the rear of the funnel, revised for one bar.
subsystems.operation: Approach the cage, guide a bar into engagement and retain it through lift.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior supplement characterizes the one-bar revision as easier to capture.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Reducing the number of simultaneous contacts can improve acquisition under yaw, but makes the captured bar and its load path more critical.
subsystems.interfaces: Cage sweep shares intake structure. Verify the final hanging pose does not load the guide as the primary structure unless intended.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test glancing hits and disable just after engagement, and inspect for bent guides after a failed grab.
subsystems.unknowns: Latch retention geometry, event installation and measured capture window.

revisions: Retained dossier reports underside shielding after riding onto algae, later curved-rack algae pickup, harness spring and one-bar cage capture.
transferable_principles: Treat moving wiring as a mechanism with a swept volume, fatigue life and failure state.
Reuse sequentially occupied volume when both functions have a clear transition and an independent load path.
disconfirming_conditions: A protected top-deck electrical bay can be preferable when an obstacle repeatedly reaches the underside or quick pit access dominates.
Shared funnel and climb packaging loses value if a bent guide compromises ordinary station cycles.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, as-built CAD, event-by-event change dates, disable-state climb behavior and end-effector controls.

recommended_images.locator: Candidate frames for later retrieval: harness spring at full lift, curved rack deployed, one-bar cage entry
